items.title: Henry David Thoreau
items.body: Henry David Thoreau worked across Ethics, Poetry, Religion, Politics, History, Biology.
items.lesson: Most so-called luxuries and comforts hinder rather than promote elevation of humankind.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Transcendentalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “I heartily accept the motto, "That government is best which governs least"; and I should like to see it acted up to more rapidly and systematically. Carried out, it finally amounts to this, which also I believe — "That government is best which governs not at all"; and when men are prepared for it, that will be the kind of government which they will have.”

items.title: Heraclitus
items.body: Heraclitus worked across Metaphysics, Epistemology, Ethics, Politics, Cosmology.
items.lesson: Everything is determined by a meeting of opposites.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pre-Socratic, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The path up and down are one and the same.”

items.title: Herbert Marcuse
items.body: Herbert Marcuse worked across Social Theory, Communism, Socialism, Industrialism, Technology.
items.lesson: In capitalist societies there is a terrifying harmony of freedom and oppression, productivity and destruction, growth and regression.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Continental Philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Man alone has the power of self-realization, the power to be a self-determining subject in all processes of becoming, for he alone has an understanding of potentialities and a knowledge of ‘notions.’ His very existence is the process of actualizing his potentialities, of molding his life according to the notions of reason.”

items.title: Herbert Spencer
items.body: Herbert Spencer worked across Politics, Sociology, Positivism, Utilitarianism.
items.lesson: Natural laws apply to all matters, without exception, to both organic and inorganic material.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Evolutionism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “There can be little question that good composition is far less dependent upon acquaintance with its laws, than upon practice and natural aptitude. A clear head, a quick imagination, and a sensitive ear, will go far towards making all rhetorical precepts needless.”

items.title: Immanuel Kant
items.body: Immanuel Kant worked across Epistemology, Metaphysics, Ethics, Cosmogony.
items.lesson: Knowledge for humans is limited by our sensory organs and brains, which are limited.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Kantianism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Act in such a way that you treat humanity, whether in your own person or in the person of any other, never merely as a means to an end, but always at the same time as an end.”

items.title: Jacques Derrida
items.body: Jacques Derrida worked across Ontology, Epistemology, Ethics, Aesthetics, Hermeneutics, Philosophy of Language.
items.lesson: Speech is different from writing; the reader is not present when we write, and the author's intentions are absent when we read.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Continental Philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “What cannot be said above all must not be silenced but written.”

items.title: Jacques Lacan
items.body: Jacques Lacan worked across Psychology.
items.lesson: By recognizing its mirror-image, the child has its first realization of itself as a unified, separate individual.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Lacanian Psychoanalysis, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The man who is born into existence deals first with language; this is a given. He is even caught in it before his birth.”

items.title: Jane Addams
items.body: Jane Addams worked across Sociology, Politics.
items.lesson: Democracy, social justice and peace are mutually reinforcing; they all have to advance together to achieve any one.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pragmatism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “We all bear traces of the starvation struggle which for so long made up the life of the race. Our very organism holds memories and glimpses of that long life of our ancestors which still goes on among so many of our contemporaries.”

items.title: Jean Baudrillard
items.body: Jean Baudrillard wrote about the economic order but also about mass communication in the post modern age. Drawing on the work of Marshall McLuhan, Baurdillard came to claim that the current age was defined by simulation: a kind of “hyperreality” where eveything is a copy without an original. Baudrillard, much like Francis Fukuyama, also thought that history had ended or “vanished,” but unlike Fukuyama, Baurdillard…
items.lesson: Marxism is merely a more efficient and equitable organization of the means of production; it does not break far enough away from capitalism.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Continental philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Simulation is no longer that of a territory, a referential being or substance. It is a generation by models of a real without origin or reality: a hyperreal.”

items.title: Jean-François Lyotard
items.body: Jean-François Lyotard worked across The Sublime, Sociology.
items.lesson: Knowledge has changed with the invention of the computer; it's now something that can be stored in databases and bought and sold.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Postmodernism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “I define postmodern as incredulity towards metanarratives.”

items.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
items.body: Jean-Jacques Rousseau worked across Political Philosophy, Music, Education, Literature.
items.lesson: In the state of nature, humans are a kind of noble savage: good, loving justice, and order.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Social Contract, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.”

items.title: Jean-Paul Sartre
items.body: Jean-Paul Sartre worked across Metaphysics, Epistemology, Ethics, Consciousness, Self-Consciousness, Literature, Political Philosophy, Ontology.
items.lesson: The content of consciousness is independent, but consciousness is always consciousness “of something.”
items.takeaway: Snapshot Existentialism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “What do we mean by saying that existence precedes essence? We mean that man first of all exists, encounters himself, surges up in the world – and defines himself afterwards.”

items.title: Jeremy Bentham
items.body: Jeremy Bentham worked across Political Philosophy, Philosophy of Law, Ethics, Economics.
items.lesson: Whether an action is right or wrong is determined by its outcome.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Utilitarianism, Legal Positivism, Liberalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Nature has placed mankind under the governance of two sovereign masters, pain and pleasure. It is for them alone to point out what we ought to do as well as to determine what we shall do.”

items.title: Johann Gottlieb Fichte
items.body: Johann Gottlieb Fichte worked across Self-Consciousness and Self-Awareness, Moral Philosophy, Political Philosophy.
items.lesson: Empirical observations cannot yield scientific laws through deduction.
items.takeaway: Snapshot German Idealism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “It is so by nature that the plant will develop with regularity, that the animal will move purposefully, and that human beings will think. Why should I take exception to recognizing also the last as the expression of an original force of nature, as I do the first and the second?”

items.title: John Dewey
items.body: John Dewey worked across Philosophy of Education, Epistemology, Ethics.
items.lesson: Humans respond to environmental conditions by developing knowledge. Practical instrumentation mediates this development.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pragmatism, Instrumentalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “As we shall see later, the most important factor in the training of good mental habits consists in acquiring the attitude of suspended conclusion, and in mastering the various methods of searching for new materials to corroborate or to refute the first suggestions that occur. To maintain the state of doubt and to carry on systematic and protracted inquiry ― these are the essentials of thinking.”

items.title: John Locke
items.body: John Locke an early proponent of universal, inalienable rights. He inspired the writing of the United States Constitution. Today, with large population movement, some question, whether, and to what extent those rights apply.
items.lesson: Human knowledge is limited by our mental faculties, and we should attempt to find that limit.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Social Contract, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The end of law is not to abolish or restrain, but to preserve and enlarge freedom.”

items.title: John Rawls
items.body: John Rawls worked across Political Philosophy, Liberalism, Justice, Politics, Social Contract Theory.
items.lesson: A rigid analytic/synthetic distinction is not useful in politics or morals.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic Philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The principles of justice are chosen behind a veil of ignorance.”

items.title: John Stuart Mill
items.body: John Stuart Mill worked across Political Philosophy, Ethics, Economics, Inductive Logic.
items.lesson: The greatest happiness of the greatest number should be what we consider when making policies.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Empiricism, Utilitarianism, Liberalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “If all mankind minus one, were of one opinion, and only one person were of the contrary opinion, mankind would be no more justified in silencing that one person, than he, if he had the power, would be justified in silencing mankind.”

items.title: Judith Butler
items.body: Judith Butler’s theory of gender has been formative to trans and queer liberation movement.
items.hook: Continental Philosophy, Third-Wave Feminism, Critical Theory, Queer Theory, Postmodernism, Post-Structuralism · (1956)
items.lesson: Language, bodily gestures, movements, and styles create the illusion of an innately gendered self.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Continental Philosophy, Third-Wave Feminism, Critical Theory, Queer Theory, Postmodernism, Post-Structuralism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “There is no gender identity behind the expressions of gender; that identity is performatively constituted by the very "expressions" that are said to be its results.”

items.title: Karl Marx
items.body: Karl Marx worked across Politics, Economics, Sociology, Labor, History, Class Struggle, Natural Sciences.
items.lesson: History is a working out of a dialectical proess operating with alienation.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Marxism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “A specter is haunting Europe—the specter of Communism.”

items.title: Karl Popper
items.body: Karl Popper worked across Epistemology, Rationality, Philosophy of Science, Logic, Social and Political Philosophy, Metaphysics, Philosophy of Mind.
items.lesson: Reality is different from human experience and cannot be accessed directly.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Critical Rationalism, Liberalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “No rational argument will have a rational effect on a man who does not want to adopt a rational attitude.”

items.title: Leo Strauss
items.body: Leo Strauss worked across Metaphysics, Epistemology, Nihilism, Politics.
items.lesson: Philosophy has been entwined with politics since the trial of Socrates.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Straussianism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Liberal relativism has its roots in the natural right tradition of tolerance or in the notion that everyone has a natural right to the pursuit of happiness as he understands happiness; but in itself it is a seminary of intolerance.”

items.title: Louis Althusser
items.body: Louis Althusser worked across Politics, Economics, Ideology.
items.lesson: There's a difference between the early work of Marx which focuses on Hegel and the late works of Marx which is more “scientific,” epitomized by Das Kapital.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Western Marxism/Structural Marxism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The sciences we are familiar with have been installed in a number of great 'continents'. Before Marx, two such continents had been opened up to scientific knowledge: the continent of Mathematics and the continent of Physics. The first by the Greeks (Thales), the second by Galileo. Marx opened up a third continent to scientific knowledge: the continent of History.”

items.title: Luce Irigaray
items.body: Luce Irigaray worked across Politics, Feminism, Language.
items.lesson: There is only one universal subject in Western culture and it is male.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Continental philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Thought excludes the heart that moves it. That which makes thought live is spoiled, set outside of it. But it does not know this.”

items.title: Ludwig Wittgenstein
items.body: Ludwig Wittgenstein worked across Logic, Metaphysics, Philosophy of Language, Philosophy of Mathematics, Philosophy of Mind, Epistemology.
items.lesson: It is not possible to talk about reality beyond our experience — this talk is nonsense.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic Philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The world is the totality of facts, not things.”

items.title: Marcus Aurelius
items.body: Marcus Aurelius worked across Politics, Ethics.
items.lesson: One should find one's place in the universe.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Stoicism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “He was a man who looked at what ought to be done, not to the reputation which is got by a man's acts”

items.title: Marshall McLuhan
items.body: Marshall McLuhan worked across Media, Technology, Sociology.
items.lesson: All media are extensions of our human senses, bodies, and minds.
items.takeaway: Snapshot New Criticism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The medium is the message.”

items.title: Martin Heidegger
items.body: Martin Heidegger worked across Ontology, Metaphysics, Art, Greek Philosophy, Technology, Language, Poetry, Thinking.
items.lesson: The main philosophical problem is being, not knowledge, as we are part of the world we investigate.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Phenomenology, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The human being is not the lord of beings, but the shepherd of Being.”

items.title: Mary Wollstonecraft
items.body: Mary Wollstonecraft worked across Feminism, Politics, Ethics.
items.lesson: All social and political relations can be explained and made transparent.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Feminism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Every political good carried to the extreme must be productive of evil.”

items.title: Maurice Merleau-Ponty
items.body: Maurice Merleau-Ponty worked across Psychology, Embodiment, Metaphysics, Perception, Gestalt Theory, Epistemology, Philosophy of Art, Western Marxism.
items.lesson: We are not ethereal centers of consciousness; we cannot sense or act without our bodies.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Phenomenology, Existential Phenomenology, Western Marxism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The world is nothing but 'world-as-meaning.'”

items.title: Max Weber
items.body: Max Weber worked across Economics, Sociology, History, Law, Politics.
items.lesson: Capitalism's growth is due in part to the Protestant work ethic.
items.takeaway: Snapshot the thinker, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The fate of our times is characterized by rationalization and intellectualization and, above all, by the disenchantment of the world.”

items.title: Michel de Montaigne
items.body: Michel de Montaigne worked across Skepticism.
items.lesson: Tranquillity depends upon detachment from the opinion of others.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Renaissance humanism, Renaissance skepticism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “I want to be seen here in my simple, natural, ordinary fashion, without straining or artifice; for it is myself that I portray...I am myself the matter of my book.”

items.title: Michel Foucault
items.body: Taking up some of the work begin by Nietzsche, Michel Foucault explored further what constitutes truth. Looking at specific domains such as sexuality, mental illness, and incarceration, Foucault describes how regimes of truth and discourses change over time. His work has been foundational to many social movements.
items.lesson: Concepts and words change over time; an archaeology of thought should be performed.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Post-Structuralism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The most defenseless tenderness and the bloodiest of powers have a similar need of confession. Western man has become a confessing animal.”

items.title: Montesquieu
items.body: Montesquieu worked across Political philosophy.
items.lesson: Despotism is an ever-present danger for any government that's not already despotic.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Classical liberalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “A man should be mourned at his birth, not at his death.”

items.title: Niccolò Machiavelli
items.body: Niccolò Machiavelli's writings have been looked to by generations of political theorists. He is also seen as an early voice advocating realpolitik. In his “Discourses on Livy,” he exposed “at times it is a very wise thing to simulate madness,” which presaged Richard Nixon’s “madman theory” of foreign policy. Many feel that the Trump Administration represents a return to madman politics.
items.lesson: The success of a nation state is paramount.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Political Realism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Since love and fear can hardly exist together, if we must choose between them, it is far safer to be feared than loved.”

items.title: Noam Chomsky
items.body: Noam Chomsky worked across Linguistics, Politics, Media.
items.lesson: If we assume that our own government is naturally more ethical than other government, we are choosing to live in a world of comforting illusion.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “States are violent to the extent that they're powerful, that's roughly accurate.”
